outcomes.text: use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of millions in real life
read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions in real life situations
read and write numbers in words up to millions for fluency
round off numbers up to the nearest hundreds of millions in real life situations

apply operations of whole numbers in real life situations
identify number sequence in different situations

appreciate use of whole numbers in real life situations

skills.name: Place value of digits up to hundreds of millions
skills.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child names the place of any digit (ones to hundred millions), including digits beside zeros, and says which digit sits in a named place. Numbers come from real settings such as a county budget or the number of phone lines.
question_forms: name the place of a digit
which digit is in a named place
how many places a number has

prerequisites.reason: Grade 7 extends the places from millions to hundred millions.
Grouping digits in threes helps to find the place.

skills.name: Total value of digits up to hundreds of millions
skills.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child gives the total value of a chosen digit (digit times its place), adds the total values of two digits, and writes the number in expanded form. The child does not mistake a digit for its total value.
question_forms: total value of an underlined digit
total values of two digits added
difference between two digits of the same value

prerequisites.reason: Total value needs the place first.
Total value to millions is already known.

skills.name: Read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions
skills.mastery: Given a number said or written in parts (for example 45 million, 12 thousand and 7) the child writes it in figures with every place filled and zero as a place holder, and reads a figure aloud in groups of three. Numbers up to 999,999,999.
question_forms: read a number aloud in groups

prerequisites.reason: The same idea, with millions as the top group.
The groups of three depend on the place of each digit.

skills.name: Write a number in words (figures to words), up to millions
skills.mastery: The child writes a number up to 9,999,999 in words with British spelling, a hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine, and each group (millions, thousands, hundreds) in order. Zeros in a group are not spoken. The design limit for words is millions.
question_forms: choose the words for a figure
write a cheque amount in words
spot the mistake in the words
say the same number two ways

prerequisites.reason: The groups of three give the words.

skills.name: Write a number in figures from words, up to millions
skills.mastery: Given a number in words up to millions, such as "two million and forty-five thousand and seven", the child writes it in figures with zero place holders in every empty place.
question_forms: order two numbers given in words

prerequisites.reason: The reverse direction, now with millions.
Writing groups of three digits with zeros.

skills.name: Round whole numbers to the nearest ten up to hundred million
skills.mastery: The child rounds a number up to 999,999,999 to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, million, ten million or hundred million: looks at the digit just to the right, rounds up on 5 or more, and writes zeros in all places after the one rounded.
question_forms: round the same number two ways

prerequisites.reason: The same rule on bigger numbers.
You must name the place to be rounded to.

skills.name: Round large numbers in news, budgets and populations
skills.mastery: Given a real setting (a population, a county budget, a news report) the child chooses the sensible place to round to, rounds the number, and says why the rounded number is only an estimate. Rounding a carried digit (such as 999,500 to the nearest thousand) is included.
question_forms: round the number in a report
why a rounded number is not exact

prerequisites.reason: The rule comes first, the setting second.

skills.name: Classify whole numbers as even or odd
skills.mastery: The child classifies any whole number up to millions as even or odd by its last digit, and knows that sums and products of even and odd numbers follow a pattern (even + even is even, odd + odd is even, even x anything is even).

skills.name: Identify prime and composite numbers up to 100
skills.mastery: The child tells prime from composite numbers up to 100 by testing small divisors, knows that 1 is neither, that 2 is the only even prime, and that an odd number is not always prime. The child lists the primes up to 50.
question_forms: pick the primes from a table

prerequisites.reason: A prime has exactly two factors.
Even numbers other than 2 are composite.
Quick tests for 5 and 10 rule out many numbers.

skills.name: Add and subtract large whole numbers (up to 9 digits)
skills.mastery: The child adds and subtracts whole numbers of up to nine digits in a column, regrouping across zeros, and decides whether to add or subtract in a story about money, population or distance. Answers are checked by estimating.
question_forms: sum or difference in a story

prerequisites.reason: Regrouping across zeros is the hard part of large subtraction.

skills.name: Multiply large whole numbers (up to 3 digits by 3 digits)
skills.mastery: The child multiplies a number of up to 4 digits by a number of up to 3 digits using long multiplication, with the zero place holder in the second and third rows, and by 10, 100 and 1,000 by shifting the digits. The product is checked by estimating.

prerequisites.reason: Extends one more digit in the multiplier.
Estimating catches a missing place holder.

skills.name: Divide large whole numbers (up to 6 digits by up to 3 digits)
skills.mastery: The child divides a number of up to 6 digits by a number of up to 3 digits by long division, with zeros in the quotient where a digit does not fit, writes the remainder as a whole number, and checks by multiplying back.
question_forms: what the remainder means in a story

prerequisites.reason: Extends the dividend by two digits.

skills.name: Work out combined operations in the correct order (with brackets)
skills.mastery: The child works out expressions of up to three operations with brackets, working brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Numbers up to 3 digits.
question_forms: put in brackets to make a value
find the mistake in the order

prerequisites.reason: Grade 6 order of operations without brackets.
Multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

skills.name: Use whole-number operations to solve real-life problems
skills.mastery: The child reads a story with two or three steps (fares, fuel, rent, bags and rows), chooses the operations, works them in order and writes the answer with its unit. Money left, total takings and equal sharing are included.

prerequisites.reason: The steps in a story give an expression to work in order.

skills.name: Find the rule of a number sequence and extend it
skills.mastery: Given the first four to six terms of a sequence with a constant difference or a constant multiplier, the child finds the rule, continues the sequence, and spots a term that does not fit.

skills.name: Find a term far along a number sequence
skills.mastery: For a sequence that goes up or down by the same amount, the child finds a distant term (for example the 12th) by first term plus the number of steps times the difference, and does not count the first term as a step.

prerequisites.reason: You need the rule to jump ahead.

skills.name: Create a number sequence from a rule
skills.mastery: Given a rule such as "start at 5, add 4" or "multiply by 3 then add 3", the child writes the first terms, and makes a sequence of their own for a number game, checking that the terms follow the rule every time.
question_forms: write the terms from a rule

prerequisites.reason: Understanding a rule comes before making one.

skills.name: Test divisibility by 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10 from the last digits
skills.mastery: The child tests a number up to 6 digits for divisibility by 2, 5 and 10 from the last digit, by 4 from the last two digits and by 8 from the last three digits, and explains the test.

prerequisites.reason: The test for 2 is the base of the tests for 4 and 8.

skills.name: Test divisibility by 3, 6 and 9 with the sum of the digits
skills.mastery: The child adds the digits of a number up to 6 digits and tests the sum for 3 and 9, and knows a number is divisible by 6 only when it is even and divisible by 3.
question_forms: divisible by 6: count from a table

prerequisites.reason: A number divisible by 6 must be even.

skills.name: Test divisibility by 11 with the alternating sum of digits
skills.mastery: The child adds the digits in the odd places and in the even places, subtracts the two sums, and says the number is divisible by 11 when the difference is 0 or a multiple of 11.
question_forms: spot the slip in the working

skills.name: Write a composite number as a product of prime factors
skills.mastery: The child splits a number up to 500 with a factor tree or repeated division by 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 until every factor is prime, writes repeated factors in full or with a power, and explains why a number with no small factors may still be composite.
question_forms: find the mistake in the working

prerequisites.reason: You need to know which numbers are prime.

skills.name: Find the GCD of numbers by the factor method
skills.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 200) as a product of primes, multiplies the primes common to all of them, taking each as many times as it is in every number, and gets the GCD.

prerequisites.reason: The factor method needs prime factors.
Grade 5 introduced the highest common factor.

skills.name: Find the LCM of numbers by the factor method
skills.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 60) as a product of primes and multiplies each prime the greatest number of times it appears in any one number, and gets the LCM.
question_forms: why the product is not the least

prerequisites.reason: The factor method needs prime factors.
Grade 5 found the LCM by listing multiples.

skills.name: Use the GCD to solve problems of cutting and packing
skills.mastery: The child decides from a story that the greatest equal size or number of equal groups is the GCD (cutting ropes, packing boxes, tiling) and works it out for two or three quantities, answering the size or the number asked.

skills.name: Use the LCM to solve problems of events that repeat together
skills.mastery: The child decides from a story that the first time two or three repeating events coincide is the LCM (matatus leaving, bells ringing) and works it out in minutes or days, answering the time asked.

skills.name: Compare and order fractions with different denominators
skills.mastery: The child compares two or three fractions with denominators up to 12 by renaming them with a common denominator, decides which is greater, orders them, and can explain why a bigger denominator does not mean a bigger fraction.

skills.name: Add fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators
skills.mastery: The child adds two fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, adds numerators, carries any whole from the fraction part, and writes the sum in simplest form.

skills.name: Subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators
skills.mastery: The child subtracts fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, regroups a whole into the fraction part when needed, reduces the whole by one, and simplifies.
question_forms: what is left in a story

skills.name: Multiply a fraction by a whole number
skills.mastery: The child multiplies a fraction by a whole number (and finds a fraction of a quantity), multiplying the numerator and keeping the denominator, simplifies, and writes an improper result as a mixed number.
question_forms: multiply a fraction by a whole number

prerequisites.reason: Repeated addition of the same fraction.

skills.name: Multiply fractions and mixed numbers
skills.mastery: The child multiplies a fraction by a fraction or a mixed number by writing mixed numbers as improper fractions, multiplying numerators and denominators, simplifying (also across before multiplying), and finds a fraction of a fraction of an amount in a story.

prerequisites.reason: Squaring a fraction is a product.
The product is simplified at the end.

skills.name: Find the reciprocal of a fraction, a whole number or a mixed number
skills.mastery: The child writes the reciprocal by turning a fraction upside down, writes a whole number as a fraction over 1 first, writes a mixed number as an improper fraction first, and checks that the number times its reciprocal is 1.
question_forms: use a reciprocal in a story

prerequisites.reason: Grade 6 found the reciprocal of proper fractions.
A whole number is a fraction over 1.

skills.name: Divide a fraction by a whole number
skills.mastery: The child divides a fraction or a mixed number by a whole number by multiplying the denominator (or by the reciprocal), simplifies, and knows the result is smaller than the fraction.
question_forms: divide a fraction by a whole number

prerequisites.reason: Dividing by a number is multiplying by its reciprocal.

skills.name: Divide by a fraction or a mixed number
skills.mastery: The child divides a whole number, fraction or mixed number by a fraction or a mixed number by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor (the second number only), writing mixed numbers as improper fractions first.
question_forms: divide a fraction by a fraction

skills.name: Divide a whole number by a fraction and use it to count how many fit
skills.mastery: The child divides a whole number by a fraction, chooses division when the story asks how many small amounts fit into a large one (cups from a jug, bags from a sack), and knows the answer is larger than the whole number.
question_forms: divide a whole number by a fraction
will the answer be larger or smaller

prerequisites.reason: The same method with a whole-number dividend.

skills.name: Continue a fraction sequence that adds or takes away the same fraction
skills.mastery: The child finds the constant gap between terms of a sequence of fractions with a common denominator, keeps the denominator, and writes the next terms and a term that is a whole number as a fraction.
question_forms: a whole number as a term

prerequisites.reason: The rule idea is the same.

skills.name: Find the rule of a fraction sequence that multiplies or divides
skills.mastery: The child finds that terms such as 1, 1/3, 1/9 follow a constant ratio, states the rule (divide by 3, or multiply by 1/3), and continues the sequence.
question_forms: spot the term that does not fit

skills.name: Use a fraction pattern in a table to answer how long it takes
skills.mastery: Given a table of the part of a task done after equal times (2, 4, 6 hours), the child finds the part done per step, and answers when the task is complete or how much is done at a later time, counting hours and not steps.

prerequisites.reason: A far term from the gap.

skills.name: Create a number sequence with fractions for a number game
skills.mastery: The child writes a sequence of fractions from a rule (add 1/4, or multiply by 1/2), keeps every term in line with the rule, and writes a rule for a puzzle sequence of their own that a partner can solve.
question_forms: write the first terms from a rule

prerequisites.reason: Understand a rule before making one.

skills.name: Find the square of a whole number
skills.mastery: The child finds the square of a whole number up to 50, and of multiples of 10 (30 squared is 900), by multiplying the number by itself, and knows that squaring is not doubling.
question_forms: square of a multiple of ten

skills.name: Find the square of a fraction
skills.mastery: The child squares a fraction by multiplying the numerator by itself and the denominator by itself, simplifies, and says why the answer is smaller than the fraction.

skills.name: Find the square of a decimal and use it for the area of a square
skills.mastery: The child squares a decimal such as 0.03 or 1.5 by multiplying without the point and giving the square twice as many decimal places, and uses it for the area of a square plot and for the area when the side is doubled.

prerequisites.reason: Squaring is multiplying a decimal by itself.

skills.name: Find the square root of a perfect square
skills.mastery: The child finds the square root of a perfect square up to 2,500 by finding the number that multiplied by itself gives it, checks by squaring, and knows the root of a sum is not the sum of the roots.

skills.name: Find the square root of a perfect-square fraction or decimal
skills.mastery: The child finds the root of a fraction by taking the root of the numerator and of the denominator (9/16 gives 3/4), and of a decimal that is a perfect square (0.09 gives 0.3 and 1.44 gives 1.2) by halving the decimal places.

prerequisites.reason: The same idea with whole numbers.
Squaring a fraction is the reverse.
Squaring a decimal doubles the places.

skills.name: Use a square root to find the side of a square plot and what follows from it
skills.mastery: The child takes the square root of the area of a square plot to find a side, then uses the side (for the distance round, or to compare plots), reading the question to know which is needed.

skills.name: Place the square root of a number between two whole numbers using perfect squares
skills.mastery: The child finds the two perfect squares either side of a number (98 lies between 81 and 100) and so places its root between two whole numbers (between 9 and 10). The number is not itself a perfect square: this skill supports checking roots.
question_forms: which perfect squares are either side
